candidates.name: File-first authoritative memory with rebuildable derived indexes
candidates.mechanism: Keep durable knowledge as human-editable Markdown in Git; treat SQLite FTS/entities/links/embeddings as disposable acceleration state that can be reconstructed.
candidates.why_it_matters: It preserves portability, auditability and tool-independence while still enabling fast hybrid retrieval.
candidates.limitations: Filesystem and index writes cannot share a real atomic transaction, so reconciliation and invariant discipline are mandatory.

candidates.name: Claim-once handoff as protocol
candidates.mechanism: Represent cross-agent continuation as persisted typed handoff state with ownership, scope, acceptance and expiry instead of relying on prose summaries alone.
candidates.why_it_matters: This turns agent switching into an explicit state transition and reduces duplicated or stale continuation context.
candidates.limitations: Correctness depends on lifecycle hooks and scope identity; unsupported clients may need explicit finalization.

candidates.name: Multi-stream retrieval with bounded authority
candidates.mechanism: Fuse lexical, entity, graph and optional vector candidates with reciprocal-rank fusion, then use small bounded metadata authority adjustments and optional reranking.
candidates.why_it_matters: It avoids betting memory quality on a single retrieval method and keeps durable canonical knowledge favored without hard-hiding episodic evidence.
candidates.limitations: More streams create tuning and explainability complexity; vector and historical modes intentionally diverge.

candidates.name: Separate learning review from live capture
candidates.mechanism: Capture synchronously only enough to persist bounded observations; run session learning in a background scheduler that stages proposals, applies policy/eval gates, retries transient failures and parks deterministic failures.
candidates.why_it_matters: The agent hot path stays reliable while the memory can still improve itself from completed work.
candidates.limitations: Auto-application increases governance requirements; provider-backed review is not zero-LLM and can export bounded context.

candidates.name: Historical recall as validity-window retrieval
candidates.mechanism: Resolve the page/entity version whose validity interval contains an as_of instant and combine version-filtered FTS with temporal entity links.
candidates.why_it_matters: It answers 'what did we know then?' instead of only searching today's rewritten memory.
candidates.limitations: Historical ranking is not a replay of the ranking that existed at that time; vectors and graph neighbors remain present-tense and are excluded.
